title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: real structures on a complex elliptic curve X = C/Λ. An antiholomorphic involution σ acts on Λ⊗R = C as an isometric reflection preserving Λ, with Q the squared length. Let P₊ be the σ-invariant sublattice with generator u, and P₋ the anti-invariant sublattice with generator e₋. There are two cases.
- Type E_a (rectangular lattice): P₊ ⊕ P₋ = Λ. Here X(R) has two components (next page).
- Type E'_a (rhombic lattice): P₊ ⊕ P₋ has index 2 in Λ, and X(R) has one component.
The invariant is a(σ) = Q(e₋)/Q(e₊). Passing from σ to −σ swaps P₊ and P₋, so a(−σ) = 1/a(σ) and the type (E or E') is preserved (previous page).

This page runs through the curves with extra automorphisms.

Square case (n = 4): e₀, e₁ are orthonormal and drawn along the diagonals of the square grid.
- Reflection in the line of e₀: invariants e₀, anti-invariants e₁. This gives type E₁ (τ = i, "2 composantes").
- Reflection in the axes: invariants e₀+e₁, anti-invariants e₀−e₁. These span an index-2 sublattice, with a' = Q(e₀−e₁)/Q(e₀+e₁) = 1. This gives type E'₁ (τ = (1+i)/2, the same curve).
So the square curve carries both an E-type and an E'-type real structure.

Hexagonal case (n = 6): u, v have |u| = |v| and an angle of 60°.
- Vertex reflections (fixing u): anti-invariants are generated by 2v−u, and ⟨u, 2v−u⟩ has index 2, so the type is E'_a with a = Q(2v−u)/Q(u).
- Face reflections are the −σ, giving E'_{1/a}.

Summary: for every curve other than the square one, the real structures form a pair {E_a, E_{1/a}} with a ≠ 1, or a pair {E'_a, E'_{1/a}}, never both. The hexagonal curve falls in the second case. The square curve has {E₁, E'₁}.

The next page converts these to moduli: τ = i√a for E_a and τ = (1+i√a)/2 for E'_a. It then computes the number of real components.

This is the classical classification of real elliptic curves (rectangular vs rhombic period lattices). It is worked out as preparatory material for the 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes' project.
errors: Hexagonal value of a is wrong. With Q(u) = Q(v) = 1 and u·v = 1/2, Q(2v−u) = 4 − 2 + 1 = 3, so a = 3, not √3. Grothendieck took the ratio of lengths instead of the ratio of Q-values. This is confirmed by the next page's formula τ = (1+i√a)/2, which gives the hexagonal τ = (1+i√3)/2 only for a = 3. Accordingly the face reflections give E'_{1/3}, not E'_{1/√3}.

Minor: the square-case text first attributes E₁ to 'symétries p.r. aux diagonales'. That is consistent only because e₀, e₁ are drawn along the diagonals of the grid; the wording is confusing but not mathematically wrong.

The summary sentence 'à l'exclusion l'un de l'autre' (for non-square curves only one type occurs) is correct but not proved on this page. It follows from a(−σ) = 1/a(σ) together with the fact that the conjugacy classes of antiholomorphic involutions are exactly σ and −σ, which the previous page established.

ideas.what: Classification of antiholomorphic involutions of C/Λ into rectangular (E_a) and rhombic (E'_a) types, with invariant a = Q(anti-invariant)/Q(invariant) and a(−σ) = 1/a(σ)
ideas.modern_name: Real structures on elliptic curves; rectangular vs rhombic lattices; real moduli Re τ = 0 or 1/2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Klein / classical (19th c.); standard in Silhol, Real Algebraic Surfaces (1989), and Alling–Greenleaf

ideas.what: Square and hexagonal curves: the square curve carries both E₁ and E'₁ structures; the hexagonal curve carries only rhombic ones (vertex vs face reflections, mutually −σ)
ideas.modern_name: Real forms of the CM elliptic curves j = 1728 and j = 0

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine, classical classification of real structures on elliptic curves, worked out as a lemma, and it contains a small arithmetic slip (√3 for 3). It is of interest only as background for the 'surface surgery' programme, with no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'et σ est donc de ce type' should read 'et −σ est donc de même type'.
'Cela correspond à [?] des symétries' is likely 'Cela correspond aux symétries p.r. aux diagonales des carrés du réseau'.
'Réflexions-faces. Ce sont [?] les [?] −σ' reads 'Ce sont les −σ, on trouve donc E'_{1/a} = E'_{1/√3}'.
The value 'a = √3' is as written in the manuscript; it is Grothendieck's error, not a transcription error (the correct value is 3).
The struck-out label before 'Réflexions-sommets' appears to be '3)' or 'a)', overwritten.
The square-case label for E₁ is probably '"2 comp."' (two real components) rather than '"2 points"'; the next page computes two connected components for E_a.
